name: Vineyard Split from Calvary Chapel
summary: The separation of John Wimber's churches from Calvary Chapel in 1982 over the place of healing, prophecy, and other 'signs and wonders' in worship, which created the Association of Vineyard Churches.

start.label: John Wimber starts a Calvary Chapel in Yorba Linda

end.label: Wimber's churches leave Calvary Chapel and join the Vineyard

background.text: Kenn Gulliksen had started 'Vineyard' fellowships within Calvary Chapel from 1974. John Wimber, a former Quaker pastor and musician, led a fast-growing Calvary Chapel in Yorba Linda from 1977.

happened.text: Wimber's church put growing emphasis on healing, prophecy, and visible manifestations of the Spirit, in contrast to Chuck Smith's focus on Bible teaching and caution about charismatic displays.

In 1982 the Calvary Chapel leadership asked Wimber to stop using the Calvary Chapel name; his churches joined Gulliksen's Vineyard fellowships, and Wimber became the leader of the Association of Vineyard Churches.
That year Wimber also taught a course on 'Signs, Wonders, and Church Growth' at Fuller Theological Seminary with C. Peter Wagner, which spread his ideas widely.

participants.name: John Wimber
participants.role: Founder and leader of the Vineyard

participants.name: Chuck Smith
participants.role: Calvary Chapel founder who asked the Vineyard churches to separate

participants.name: Kenn Gulliksen
participants.role: Founder of the first Vineyard fellowships

participants.name: C. Peter Wagner
participants.role: Fuller professor who co-taught Wimber's course

outcomes.text: The Vineyard grew into an international movement of some 2,000+ churches and a major source of contemporary worship music.
In 1995 the Vineyard itself removed the Toronto Airport Vineyard after the 'Toronto Blessing' revival, over manifestations it judged excessive.

condemnations.reason: Toronto Airport Vineyard disaffiliated over the manifestations of the 'Toronto Blessing'
condemnations.status: Became Toronto Airport Christian Fellowship (later Catch the Fire)

persecution_note: No one was persecuted; the split was a parting of ways between church leaders.

sources.citation: Bill Jackson, The Quest for the Radical Middle: A History of the Vineyard. Cape Town: Vineyard International Publishing, 1999.
